section_summary: The section opens with a July 1941 Radio Tokyo bulletin listing shortwave schedules, frequencies, languages, and programme highlights for audiences around the world. It then contains an FBI cover letter and English transcriptions of Japanese-language broadcasts from Station JZK for June 10–15, 1941. The broadcasts cover Japan’s negotiations with the Dutch East Indies and Soviet Union, the Nanking government, fighting in China, the war in Syria, and commentary promoting Japan’s “new order” in East Asia.

subfiles.title: Radio Tokyo July 1941 programme bulletin
subfiles.from: Nippon Hoso Kyokai, Broadcasting Corporation of Japan
subfiles.about: July schedules and promotional notices describe Radio Tokyo’s shortwave services for audiences in multiple regions and languages.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin gives transmission times, frequencies, news slots, talks, music, and July programme highlights. It includes Italian daily listings and French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Malay, Dutch, and other audience notices, followed by announcements of advance weekly programme listings.

subfiles.title: FBI forwarding letter to Adolf A. Berle Jr.
subfiles.about: Hoover forwards Japanese-language Station JZK broadcast transcriptions for June 10–18, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Forwards JZK transcriptions as possibly of interest.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 10, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: News and commentary address Dutch East Indies talks, fighting in China and Syria, and the campaign to “Japanize” national life.
subfiles.summary: The news reports a firm Japanese stance toward the Dutch East Indies, an East Asian organization, military operations in China, and European war developments. A long commentary presents racial solidarity, science, education, religion, and culture as parts of a “Japanized” national life. The programme closes with poetry and music.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 11, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The broadcast covers a cabinet appointment, Dutch East Indies negotiations, China fighting, and Britain’s attack on Syria.
subfiles.summary: News describes Ino’s appointment as agriculture minister, Japan’s position toward the Dutch East Indies, and fighting in China and the Near East. The main commentary argues that Britain’s invasion of Syria will weaken its position and widen the war. A final talk praises Japanese operations in Shanxi.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 12, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The programme reports Japan–Soviet trade terms and promotes the planned Rising Asia League.
subfiles.summary: News details proposed trade and payment agreements with the Soviet Union, the Dutch East Indies negotiations, events in China, and fighting in Syria. The main commentary praises consolidation of Japanese organizations into the Rising Asia League as a means of creating a new order in East Asia. A second talk promotes the Nanking government and Japanese military assistance to it.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 13, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The broadcast welcomes the Japan–Soviet trade agreement and reports war news from China, Syria, and Europe.
subfiles.summary: News emphasizes the announced Japan–Soviet agreement, conditions in Chongqing, the Dutch East Indies dispute, and Axis accounts of the European and Syrian campaigns. A lengthy commentary traces the negotiations and explains the agreement’s trade, payment, and renewal terms while presenting it as a diplomatic success for Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 14, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The programme focuses on Wang Jingwei’s visit to Japan and presents Japanese operations against Chongqing as successful.
subfiles.summary: News describes Wang Jingwei’s itinerary and Japanese discussions about strengthening the Nanking government, alongside the Dutch East Indies dispute, naval restrictions, and European war reports. Commentary claims that air attacks and blocked transport routes are weakening Chongqing. A closing segment for listeners in Hawaii discusses rice planting, triplets, and plans to record combat sounds.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme transcription, June 15, 1941
subfiles.from: Station JZK, Tokyo; transcribed by the Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: News covers Japanese attacks in China, Wang Jingwei’s journey, Syria, and Axis diplomatic and military contacts.
subfiles.summary: The broadcast reports further Japanese raids in China, alleged conflict between Chongqing and Communist forces, and Japanese newspaper support for Wang Jingwei’s visit. It also relays Vichy and Italian accounts of the war, a Japanese military delegation’s visit to Italy, Ribbentrop’s trip to Venice, and Ambassador Nomura’s Washington meeting. The transcription continues beyond page 220.
